conventions.convention: Signature is (−,+,+,+), orientation is independent of time orientation, coordinates use x⁰=ct, κ=8πG_N/c⁴, and the sourced Maxwell sign is ∇ₐFᵃᵇ=−μ₀jᵇ.
A is a global real potential, F=dA, φ is a global complex scalar, the charged derivative is ∂ₐφ−iλAₐφ, and λ is any real number. Nontrivial bundle sectors and singular sources are excluded.

The finite-regularity domain retains a smooth underlying manifold but permits g∈C³ and A,φ∈C². Actions are integrals of compact density differences when global integrals are not finite; independent variation directions are smooth and compactly supported.
Temporal gauge means A₀=0. The scalar symmetric reduction requires g⁰⁰<0 and positive-definite inverse spatial block (gⁱʲ). Complex unknowns are split into real and imaginary components.

D denotes the spatial Levi-Civita derivative, while the charged derivative is denoted separately. In a positive future orthonormal frame F₀ᵢ=−eᵢ, Fᵢⱼ=εᵢⱼₖbₖ, ε₁₂₃=1, and j⁰=−nₐjᵃ. Maxwell evolution uses normal contractions, including shift contributions to coordinate-time residuals.

The periodic theorem assumes AC_ω and DC, integer s≥5, h and φ₀ in H^{s+1}, remaining complete data in H^s, exact spatial-potential compatibility, charged scalar compatibility, all Maxwell and total-stress Einstein constraints, and compact admissible state bounds. Smooth geometric uniqueness includes a real gauge function vanishing on the initial surface.

This holds for smooth solutions and for the explicitly stated classical finite-regularity class.

The stated off-shell current and stress identities hold, and the scalar and sourced Maxwell equations imply total-stress conservation before any Einstein equation is used.

After eliminating the spatial compatibility time derivatives from the scalar divergence equation, the stated temporal-gauge scalar principal matrices are symmetric and their time matrix is positive definite under g⁰⁰<0 and (gⁱʲ)>0; the scalar and potential transport equations add identity time blocks and no spatial derivative blocks.

Under its complete periodic data, compatibility, constraint, choice and admissible-state hypotheses, there is a local solution of the full Einstein, sourced Maxwell and classical charged-scalar equations with the stated Sobolev regularity and constraint propagation; smooth data persist smoothly on the same interval. Complete constrained smooth data on a general smooth oriented boundaryless initial three-manifold have local smooth developments, with the stated data-fixing isometry and global real gauge equivalence near the initial surface.
